item.title: Xi stresses China-UK cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Xi stresses China-UK cooperation In phone talks with Burnham, he notes two countries' broad common interests President Xi Jinping has called on China and the United Kingdom to respect and trust each other, transcend disagreements, seek common ground while reserving differences and make the pie of mutually beneficial cooperation even bigger. Xi made the remarks in phone talks with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Tuesday. This marked their first interaction since Burnham took office in July. Xi, who congratulated Burnham on assuming office as UK prime minister, noted that China and the UK are comprehensive strategic partners, and stressed that despite their different social systems and national conditions, the two countries share more common interests than differences. As both governments are committed to developing the economy and improving people's livelihoods, they can draw on their respective strengths and provide mutual support, he added. Xi said that during its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period, China will further expand opening-up in sectors such as education, healthcare and finance, which he described as areas with great potential for bilateral cooperation. He added that as major countries in science and technology with rich resources in education, culture and sports, China and the UK should maintain an open and forward-looking perspective, and strengthen exchanges and cooperation across all fields. Xi also expressed his hope that the UK will fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese investors. Regarding multilateral affairs, Xi underscored that the two countries are both permanent members of the United Nations Security Council and major economies in the world, and they both support multilateralism and open trade and uphold the central role of the UN. He called for joint efforts to strengthen communication and cooperation within frameworks such as the UN, the G20 and the World Trade Organization, in order to promote an equal and orderly multipolar world as well as universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization. Burnham welcomed Xi's views and recalled that during his tenure as mayor of Greater Manchester, he had maintained many years of friendly exchanges with China. President Xi made a state visit to the UK in 2015, which included a trip to Manchester. This, Burnham said, has had a significant impact on promoting exchanges and cooperation between the local community and the Chinese side. The UK will maintain continuity in its China policy and is firmly committed to developing a long-term and consistent UK-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Burnham said. He expressed the UK's readiness to engage in high-level exchanges with China, advance bilateral cooperation across all fields and strengthen people-to-people ties, in an effort to restore bilateral relations to their historical high level and bring greater benefits to the two peoples. Burnham reaffirmed that the UK's position on the Taiwan question remains unchanged. Amid the current volatile and complex international landscape, the UK and China, as permanent members of the UN Security Council, should promote dialogue to resolve international hot spot issues and jointly address global challenges such as climate change, in order to safeguard world stability and prosperity, he said. Burnham also commended China's efficient and effective response to the mudslide that struck Gyirong county in the Xizang autonomous region, while expressing his appreciation to China for assisting UK citizens who were affected. The two leaders agreed to stay in touch and said that dialogue between their governments on a range of mutual priorities would continue, according to a news release issued by the British Prime Minister's Office after the phone talks.

item.title: Nubia readies for AI-agent smartphone
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Nubia readies for AI-agent smartphone Launch of NaviX Ultra represents 'phone itself an intelligent assistant' ZTE's smartphone brand Nubia is set to release its NaviX Ultra on Sept 16, a device it calls the world's first mass-produced artificial intelligence-agent smartphone, marking a major step in the commercial rollout of on-device AI models in China. The NaviX Ultra is powered by ByteDance's Doubao AI Phone Assistant, integrating the AI model at the system level rather than as a stand-alone app. Users interact with the embedded AI via voice or a dedicated orange physical button. "The essential difference is this: previous AI phones were 'hardware with AI features tacked on'. An AI-agent phone has the phone itself becoming an intelligent assistant," said Ni Fei, president of ZTE's terminal business division. The device is built around four core capabilities: understanding natural language, executing tasks across apps, remembering user preferences and ensuring security. Its system-level Graphical User Interface agent architecture can interpret on-screen content and simulate humanlike taps and swipes to complete multistep tasks across applications — all through a single voice command. For example, users can ask the phone to compare prices, fill in order forms and complete payments without manually switching between apps. The device received network access approval from China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology on Sept 1, completing the full compliance process from large language model filing to terminal certification. Crucially, core AI model computations run entirely on-device, meaning user data does not need to be uploaded to the cloud — a design that significantly reduces privacy risks, Nubia said. The NaviX Ultra builds on lessons learned from the Nubia M153, a limited-edition engineering prototype released in December that sold out quickly and saw significant markups on the secondary market. That earlier device used a technique to simulate human touch on apps — which eventually led to being blocked by major platforms. For the NaviX Ultra, Nubia and ByteDance have shifted to standardized Model Context Protocol and A2A protocols, moving from "forced entry to requested access". The handset now requires partner apps to proactively provide MCP services and open up data and operational capabilities before the Doubao assistant can interface with them. More than 10 partner platforms — including Douyin, Luckin Coffee, Qunar, Meituan and Didi — are already integrated. "The year 2026 can be regarded as the 'first year of the agent smartphone'," said Lin Keyu, a senior analyst at Counterpoint Research. The launch comes as the broader smartphone market faces headwinds. IDC forecasts that global smartphone shipments could decline 13.9 percent year-on-year in 2026, driven by memory shortages and other factors. Yet within this challenging environment, AI is emerging as a key differentiator. IDC forecasts that AI-capable phones will account for 53 percent of China's smartphone market in 2026, with shipments reaching 147 million units. CITIC Securities said in a research report that AI agents represent a core scenario for AI application deployment, and their proliferation on end-devices will drive a revaluation of the entire consumer electronics supply chain.

item.title: Nation ready to unite forces to safeguard 'blue home'
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Nation ready to unite forces to safeguard 'blue home' China is ready to strengthen cooperation with all sides to jointly protect "our blue home" and build a brighter shared future for the maritime community, a senior official said on Tuesday. He Guangshun, chief engineer at the Ministry of Natural Resources, made the remarks during the opening ceremony of the high-level meeting of the 22nd Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies Meeting in Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province. Outlining the nation's progress in the maritime sector, He said that China has launched a pilot program in recent years to identify marine carbon sinks and assign monetary value to the carbon captured by coastal ecosystems, including its expanding mangrove forests, seagrass beds and seaweed farms. Marine carbon sinks refer to coastal and deep-ocean environments that absorb and store atmospheric carbon dioxide within their biomass and underlying sediments. The senior official emphasized China's commitment to protecting the marine environment through its participation in relevant international treaties and frameworks, and called for coordinated action to address rising sea levels and biodiversity loss. Noting that China has signed cooperation agreements with over 50 countries and international organizations and has launched more than 100 related projects, He called on other Asian coast guard agencies to help safeguard their shared "blue home". During the meeting, the China Coast Guard presented its new marine carbon sink law enforcement model. The framework requires maritime polluters to remedy ecological damage and restore the ocean's carbon sequestration capacity, marking a shift from a traditional punishment-focused approach to maritime supervision. Following the opening ceremony, a 90-minute special session featuring academic presentations elaborated on the new enforcement model. Zhao Yingfei, a China Coast Guard law enforcement officer who moderated the session, said on the sidelines of the meeting that the agency is moving beyond punishment-focused maritime policing to fully implement the new model. She said that the framework leverages legal measures to quantify ecological harm from maritime violations and mandate targeted ecological restoration by responsible parties. Domestically, the mechanism safeguards China's marine ecological environment and advances sustainable growth for maritime industries, Zhao said, adding that internationally, it marks China's proactive contribution to global ocean governance. The China Coast Guard plans to fully embed the updated enforcement approach into all front-line maritime operations. Wang Kaiqiang, deputy director of the China Coast Guard, said that the high-level meeting served as a key platform to showcase the carbon sink law enforcement model as a benchmark for modern ocean governance worldwide. "We must adopt a holistic approach that addresses both the symptoms and root causes of maritime risks," Wang said, calling for closer practical cooperation to build a tighter maritime community with a shared future. The agenda for this year's meeting included crackdown on illegal maritime activities, search-and-rescue operations, marine ecological protection, information sharing, joint drills and capacity building. Apart from the special session on maritime carbon sink law enforcement, the meeting also featured a dedicated session on the Global Security Initiative, designed to strengthen regional ocean governance and address common maritime challenges. Liu Zhixu, head of the China Coast Guard law enforcement department's international cooperation division, said that the special briefing aimed to advance the vision of a "maritime community with a shared future" and to share practical experience in balancing maritime security and ecological protection. Liu noted that the innovative meeting arrangements reflected China's foresight and exemplary role in "blue governance", establishing the country as a forward-thinking partner in regional maritime cooperation. The organizers said that the high-level meeting had brought together delegates from 23 countries and regions, as well as two international organizations. This year marked China's first time organizing the high-level meeting, following its chairing of the North Pacific Coast Guard Forum last year.

item.title: Squeezable toys relieve student, staff stress
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Squeezable toys relieve student, staff stress Chinese novelties firm looking for different growth path from Pop Mart In a shopping mall in Hopson One Mall in Yangpu district, Shanghai, hundreds of visitors line up at a popup store. They are drawn by a popular item — squishy cake toys — colorful, foam squeezables designed for stress relief and fashion statements. Unlike ultra-squishy toys, this item has a firmer foam texture, great for office desk decor, party gifts or relieving work and school pressure for both kids and adults alike. The squishy cake toy comes in a variety of scrumptious shapes — strawberry, cherry, croissant and mushroom. Each of them is priced at around 25 yuan ($3.7). "I bought three squishy cake toys today. I like the soft touch of the toys. It is very stress-relieving," said Zhang Le, a 30-year-old designer in Shanghai. "I took my daughter to the pop-up store here. She likes squishy cake toys very much. She often shares the toys with her classmate. I bought five for her and one for myself. I can put the squishy cake toy on my office desk. It puts me in a good mood," said Cheng Yuqi, a 45-year-old mother in Shanghai. Since July, another style of squishy cake toys produced by Shanghai local brand Molynk have gone viral on TikTok. Related videos have already topped 180 million views. The product, priced at 299 yuan, sold out soon after its global debut, with 5,000 units purchased. The toys have become so popular that a large number of tourists from Southeast Asian countries such as Thailand are paying special visits to China, dragging their suitcases to offline stores in Shanghai for shopping trips. After these tourists return to their home countries, even if they resell their products at double or even higher prices, the products are still highly sought after by local consumers, as reported by Xinmin.cn. At a soft rubber toy factory in Zhejiang province's Yiwu, located some 300 kilometers from Shanghai, millions of "freshly baked" bun-shaped decompression toys are about to board a truck bound for Ningbo Zhoushan Port, crossing mountains and waterways to Europe and North America. The latest data released by the General Administration of Customs of China showed that the total export value of Chinese toys in the first half was $15.6 billion, with some markets showing a recovery trend. Behind this evolving phenomenon of exports is a synergy of multiple factors, such as "China-Chic" design breakthroughs, mature supply chain support, global layout acceleration and the enduring and increasing appeal of emotional consumption. In recent years, the global emotional consumption market has continued to heat up, and stress relieving games and items have formed a billion dollar gold mine. According to the Global Stress Relief Toy Special Report issued by Verified Market Research, the global stress relief toy market is expected to reach $6.26 billion by 2026, and is projected to surpass $8.96 billion by 2030. Li Weiqing, founder and CEO of Molynk — one of the producers of squishy cake toys — said: "Since our establishment, the brand has aimed for a global layout. This may be different from Pop Mart, which was born in China and gradually achieved globalization with later development. When we were founded, we deployed branch offices in the United States, Japan and Spain, with Shanghai as our headquarters." Li Yun, general manager of Unie Toys in Minhang district, Shanghai, said: "We found the soft, colorful squishy cake toys well-received by consumers, both kids and adults. With the accelerated pace of modern life, people are increasingly placing emphasis on things that offer emotional value." Dong Peng, an independent senior analyst, said: "Shanghai squishy cake toys have gone from low-end OEM to cross-border hard currency, essentially completing the cognitive upgrade from 'emotional consumer goods' to 'cultural symbol carriers', no longer relying on simple price differences, but on precise translation and efficient supply of contemporary people's emotional needs."

item.title: South Korean businesses eye China tie-ups
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
South Korean businesses eye China tie-ups Experts expect Shenzhen APEC to boost tech cooperation with Busan Companies in Busan, a major industrial and logistics hub in South Korea, are increasingly seeing China not merely as a production base but as a partner for technology cooperation and supply chain integration, experts said. They told China Daily that the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in South China's Guangdong province in November will serve as a catalyst, attracting more business interest in the city regarded as the window of China's opening-up. "The interest (from the Busan business community in Shenzhen) has clearly increased," said Jung Hyun-min, former vice-mayor of Busan and executive vice-president of Busan Chamber of Commerce and Industry. "It is not a temporary trend but a structural shift driven by global supply chain restructuring, technological competition and market diversification," Jung said. Following last year's gathering in Gyeongju, a city 30 minutes from Busan by train, the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting will take place in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19, under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together". China has been South Korea's largest trading partner for over two decades, with bilateral trade continuing to expand amid industrial-chain integration. In the first half of 2026, bilateral trade reached $231.33 billion, increasing 47.7 percent year-on-year, according to Chinese customs data. Jung said Shenzhen, which focuses on innovation and leads in digital transformation, naturally attracts companies from Busan as it is a practical partner for those looking to cooperate with China. This is because of Shenzhen's unique strength in seamlessly connecting research and development, manufacturing, investment, logistics, and the overseas market within one city cluster, he said. Since 2022, Shenzhen's total industrial output above designated size and industrial added value have ranked first among Chinese cities, according to Shenzhen Daily. The city's total research and development expenditure reached 245.3 billion yuan ($36.5 billion) in 2024, with corporate R&D accounting for more than 93 percent, also ranking first nationwide. "For South Korean companies, especially the tech-based small and medium-sized enterprises in South Korea, this framework is crucial, as the speed of validating an idea directly determines their survival," said Jung. For example, he noted that the Huaqiangbei parts industry chain in Shenzhen demonstrates remarkable development and validation speed, with some companies even completing prototypes in merely one to two weeks. Noting that Busan is the world's second-largest transshipment port and part of a major manufacturing cluster in South Korea, Kim Youngjae, president of the Busan Development Institute and the Busan-China Business Forum, said Busan and Shenzhen can complement each other, with Shenzhen supplying advanced components and Busan offering physical test beds. He said the heads-of-state's bilateral meeting on the sidelines of last year's APEC gathering in South Korea paved the way for renewed economic dialogue. "If Busan companies form cooperation with those in Shenzhen, I think it could help them not only utilize those technologies, but also open up new markets," Kim said. Jung, from the Busan Chamber of Commerce and Industry, also said cooperation between the two cities can extend beyond trade into third countries and regional supply chain integration under the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, the world's largest free trade agreement, to which both South Korea and China are signatories. However, Jung said Busan companies also face various challenges in cooperating with their Chinese peers. These include information asymmetry across the diverse Chinese market, difficulty finding trustworthy partners, barriers such as certification and legal issues, and uncertainty from China-US tensions. Innovation ecosystem In response, Jung said the chamber established a formal cooperative relationship with the Shenzhen International Chamber of Commerce, laying the foundation for connecting with China's innovation ecosystem and promoting cross-border economic and trade collaboration. Moreover, Jung said the cooperation should not be limited to Shenzhen but could also involve other Chinese cities such as the port city of Ningbo, Southwest China's Chengdu, and Shanghai to create greater synergy, involving innovation, maritime logistics, the inland market, finance, and platforms. As the South Korean government has put great emphasis on semiconductors and physical artificial intelligence, with Busan and neighboring regions among those to host such projects, Kim said it will also provide opportunities for cooperation in clean energy and the high-tech industrial ecosystem. He also stressed the importance of people-to-people exchanges in laying the foundation for business cooperation, as it can help narrow the information gap and enhance mutual understanding. "Listening to recent news from the Chinese central government as well as Shenzhen, China is investing heavily in AI … South Korean companies cannot afford to ignore these developments," said Kim.

item.title: Changsha's stinky tofu draws crowds with its funky charm
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Changsha's stinky tofu draws crowds with its funky charm Centuries-old snack assaults the nose, but conquers the taste buds The smell can be a bit overpowering, even off-putting. But one bite and you are hooked. That is the magic of stinky tofu in Changsha, Hunan province — a snack that has captivated locals and tourists alike for more than 200 years. "I grew up on this," said Shi Xukui, a 30-year-old office worker in Changsha. "It's not fancy. You stand by the cart, bite into it while it's piping hot, and the juice runs down your chin — that's the real taste of the city." Stinky tofu in Changsha is not just a snack — it's a dare, a comfort, a collective childhood memory and a daily delight. It assaults your nose way before it even reaches your lips: The aroma — pungent, earthy and deeply fermented — hits you from half a block away. However, the smell is only the opening act. Once the black cubes hit the sizzling oil at 150 C, they transform into a smoky, savory seduction that draws crowds like a magnet. Bite through the crackling shell, and a hot, spicy, garlic-laced broth explodes in your mouth — juicy, messy and utterly addictive. But here's the beauty of Changsha: No two batches of the delicacy taste exactly the same. At Fire God Palace (Huo Gong Dian) — a historic temple now turned into a time-honored dining destination known for traditional Hunan snacks — the brine is made from a secret family recipe and aged for two years. At Hey Hey Black, which has outlets everywhere, the seasoning packs a stronger punch with a chili kick that wakes up your palate. Then there are the nameless corner stalls. Vendors set up their carts at dusk, offering a comforting escape for workers and students weary after a whole day's labor. At about 2 yuan (30 US cents) a pop, it's an affordable thrill that appeals to all ages and income groups. The craft of making Fire God Palace stinky tofu has been recognized as a national intangible cultural heritage, said Zhou Houmu, a fourth-generation inheritor at Fire God Palace, who has been making it for over 17 years. Zhou said the process involves five steps: selecting the brine ingredients, making the brine, preparing the tofu curd, soaking the curd in the brine and deep-frying it. The brine is the heart of it all — a blend of more than 20 ingredients, including mushrooms, winter bamboo shoots, black fermented soybeans and perilla leaves. It ferments naturally for 18 months to two years, he said. "It's the brine that makes all the difference," Zhou said. "That's why our stinky tofu smells funky but tastes delicious." The proof lies in the eating. Liu Fei, 60, a visitor from Hebei province who grew up in Changsha, returned to the city recently with his family to revisit his childhood memories. "I've had stinky tofu in other places, but none of them compare to this," he said. "This is the most authentic you can get." Damon Shelby, a 27-year-old from the United States who is visiting Changsha, was equally smitten. "My first impression was that it was really moist, with lots of flavor all at once," he said. "I liked how juicy it was. It's interesting that it's black — we don't have anything like this in America. I feel it's really good to eat while you're walking." Long Shixing, head of operations at Fire God Palace, said the outlet sells about 4 million pieces of stinky tofu each year and has drawn over 7.22 million visitors so far this year. The rush typically peaks between 4 pm and 9 pm, when Changsha's vibrant nightlife comes alive, he said. Stinky tofu has become a signature of Changsha's food culture, said Zhou, the inheritor. "When you go out for a late-night snack in Changsha, you have to order a portion. It's like you haven't really been to Changsha if you haven't tried it."

item.title: Neighbors give Lao hospitals healthy dose of support
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
Neighbors give Lao hospitals healthy dose of support Cross-border care, training and medical exchanges boost patients' treatment options Laoportor, 42, recently crossed the border from Laos into southwestern China's Yunnan province for medical treatment after local doctors failed to resolve his health problems. The resident of a northern province of Laos was treated at a local hospital for several days for bile duct stones and liver-related issues. But his condition showed little improvement. On the advice of a Lao doctor, he traveled to Mengla County People's Hospital in Xishuangbanna Dai autonomous prefecture for further treatment. After spending a day and a night at the hospital, Laoportor said he felt much better. When interviewed by China Daily recently, he was still weak and remained in bed with his wife at his side. He said he was gradually recovering. "I am very grateful to the medical team here," he said. "The service and facilities are good, and the medical team is highly skilled. When I go back, I will recommend the hospital to people I know." Laoportor is far from alone. Xishuangbanna shares a 677-kilometer border with Laos. Six townships and 14 villages lie along the frontier. Mengla County People's Hospital received more than 13,000 foreign patients in 2025, compared with about 500 in 2013, according to Miao Zhihai, Party secretary of the hospital. Lao nationals accounted for 97.5 percent of its foreign patients last year. What began largely with emergency and critical cases has expanded to include chronic disease treatment, maternal and child healthcare, health checks and disease prevention, Miao said. Across Xishuangbanna, public medical institutions treated more than 30,000 foreign patients in 2025, according to the prefecture's health commission. But the growing flow of patients into China tells only part of the story. Along the border, Chinese medical services and expertise are being extended into Laos so more patients can be treated closer to home. However, this raises a practical question: can cross-border healthcare grow without putting pressure on Chinese medical resources? Hospital officials told China Daily the current number of foreign patients remains within the hospital system's capacity without affecting services for local residents.

item.title: Embrace of cultures still best lesson on understanding
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-08
Embrace of cultures still best lesson on understanding Renowned educator's return visit sheds light on positive results of exchanges When Ronald Sakolsky walked into a conference room in Beijing recently, he was immediately greeted by a former student he hadn't seen in 26 years. The embrace that followed — captured by cameras and shared across social media — became yet another symbol of the enduring power of people-to-people connections between China and the United States. Sakolsky, a retired history teacher from Pennsylvania, was in China for a 10-day visit from Aug 23 to Sept 1 at the invitation of the China Education Association for International Exchange. His journey — from Beijing to the Inner Mongolia autonomous region and Henan province — brought together the threads of a story that began in 1999, when he first came to Henan's Luoyang via a teacher exchange program that would ultimately transform hundreds of lives on both sides of the Pacific. The US-China Teachers Exchange Program operated from 1996 to 2014. It was run jointly by the China Education Association for International Exchange and the American Council of Learned Societies, which was later replaced by the National Committee on US-China Relations. During the 18 years, the program sent 332 Chinese teachers to schools across the US and brought 117 American teachers to Chinese classrooms. Margot Landman, former program director and deputy vice president of the NCUSCR, said what began as "a crazy idea, unclear in the details" grew into a bridge of understanding that continues to bear fruit long after the formal exchanges ended.
